# Introduction

 This mini project's goal is to explore relationships between energy consumption, carbon emissions and public transportation across the U.S. The project identifies transit agencies that stand out for their energy consumption patterns, emissions efficiency, and estimated emissions avoided. Overall, the goal is to better understand how public transportation contributes to energy use and environmental sustainability in the United States.

## Task One A: Data Acquisition
This first dataset is collected from the U.S. Energy Information Administration's State Energy Profiles.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}


EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

## Task One B: Data Acquisition
The second dataset was obtained from the National Transit Database using an API request.
```{r}
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate), state_full = str_to_title(str_trim(state)))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

## Task One C: Data Acquisition
The third dataset was downloaded from the National Transit Database's 2025 Energy Consumption Report.
```{r}
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```


## Task Two: Data Cleaning and Preparation
The three datasets were examined using structure and summary functions to understand their variables and identify inconsistencies. Transportation mode codes were converted into full descriptive names using a lookup table created with recode(), making my results easier to interpret.

```{r}
str(EIA_SEP_REPORT)
str(NTD_ENERGY)
str(NTD_SERVICE)

NTD_ENERGY |>
  distinct(Mode) |>
  arrange(Mode)

NTD_SERVICE |>
  distinct(mode) |>
  arrange(mode)

NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    Mode = recode(
      Mode,
      "HR" = "Heavy Rail",
      "LR" = "Light Rail",
      "CR" = "Commuter Rail",
      "MB" = "Motor Bus",
      "CB" = "Commuter Bus",
      "RB" = "Bus Rapid Transit",
      "TB" = "Trolleybus",
      "DR" = "Demand Response",
      "DT" = "Demand Response Taxi",
      "VP" = "Vanpool",
      "FB" = "Ferryboat",
      "SR" = "Streetcar Rail",
      "AR" = "Alaska Railroad",
      "CC" = "Cable Car",
      "MG" = "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
      "IP" = "Inclined Plane",
      "TR" = "Aerial Tramway",
      "YR" = "Hybrid Rail",
      .default = "Unknown"
    )
  )

NTD_ENERGY |>
  count(Mode, sort = TRUE)
  
  NTD_ENERGY |>
  filter(Mode == "Unknown") |>
  distinct(Mode)
```

## Task Three: Data Integration and Initial Exploration
### 1. Which five states have the most expensive retail electricity?

```{r}
top5_electricity_prices <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(electricity_price_MWh)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

top5_electricity_prices
library (scales)
ggplot(
  top5_electricity_prices,
  aes(x = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh),
    y = electricity_price_MWh)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2878B5", width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "The Five Most Expensive States for Electricity",
    subtitle = "Average retail electricity price per 1,000 kWh",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Electricity price ($)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```
The EIA dataset was sorted by average retail electricity price in descending order, and the five states with the highest prices were selected. A horizontal bar chart was created to make the differences easier to compare. Hawaii had the highest average electricity price at $380 per MWh, followed by California, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.

### 2. Which 5 states have the ‘dirtiest’ electricity mix?

```{r}
library(gt)
top5_dirty_states <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(CO2_MWh)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  select(
    state,
    abbreviation,
    primary_source,
    CO2_MWh) |>
  mutate(
    CO2_MWh = comma(CO2_MWh))

top5_dirty_states |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Five States with the Highest Electricity Emissions",
    subtitle = "Pounds of CO2 emitted per MWh") |>
  cols_label(
    state = "State",
    abbreviation = "Abbreviation",
    primary_source = "Primary Energy Source",
    CO2_MWh = "CO2 Emissions (lbs/MWh)")
```
The states were ranked according to carbon dioxide emissions per megawatt-hour of electricity generated. The five highest-emitting states were selected and displayed in a formatted table using the gt package. West Virginia had the highest emissions at 1,912 pounds of CO2 per MWh, followed by Kentucky, Wyoming, Missouri, and Hawaii.

### 3. On average, how many pounds of CO2 are emitted per MWh of electricity produced in the US?

```{r}
US_CO2_average <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  summarize(total_emissions = sum(CO2_MWh * generation_MWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_generation = sum(generation_MWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    weighted_average = total_emissions / total_generation)

US_CO2_average
```
There are 784.8 pounds of CO2 emitted per MWh. I calculated the weighted average using each state's carbon emissions per MWh multiplied by its total electricity generation, then I added the values and divided them by total electricity generation across all 50 states. 

### 4. What are the three rarest primary energy sources in the US? What is the associated cost of electricity associated with each source and in what states are they used?

```{r}
rare_electricity_sources <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  group_by(primary_source) |>
  summarize(
    number_of_states = n(),
    average_price = mean(
      electricity_price_MWh,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    states = paste(sort(state),
      collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(number_of_states) |>
  slice_head(n = 3)

rare_electricity_sources

rare_electricity_sources |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "The Rarest Primary Electricity Sources",
    subtitle = "Based on the number of states using each source") |>
  cols_label(
    primary_source = "Energy Source",
    number_of_states = "Number of States",
    average_price = "Average Electricity Price ($)",
    states = "States") |>
  fmt_currency(
    columns = average_price,
    decimals = 2
  )
```
Petroleum was the rarest source, appearing in only Hawaii. Hydroelectric power and wind were each reported in four states.

### 5. How many times cleaner is NY’s energy mix than that of Texas? 

```{r}
ny_texas <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  filter(abbreviation %in% c("NY", "TX")) |>
  select(state, abbreviation, CO2_MWh)

ny_CO2 <- ny_texas|>
  filter(abbreviation == "NY") |>
  pull(CO2_MWh)

tx_CO2 <- ny_texas |>
  filter(abbreviation == "TX") |>
  pull(CO2_MWh)

cleaner_state <- tx_CO2 / ny_CO2
cleaner_state
```
#### Texas produces approximately 1.53 times as much CO2 per MWh as New York.

New York's electricity mix is approximately 1.53 times cleaner than Texas's based on CO2 emissions per MWh of electricity generated.

### 6. Which five transit agencies used the most gallons of fuel (all sources) and how did it breakdown by type?

```{r}
energy_columns <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  select(starts_with("Gallons of")) |>
  names()

energy_columns

NTD_ENERGY |>
  select(
    starts_with("Gallons of"),
    starts_with("Kilowatt hours"),
    starts_with("Kilograms")) |>
  glimpse()
  
  top5_fuel_agencies <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      all_of(energy_columns),
      ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    total_gallons = sum(
      c_across(all_of(energy_columns)), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(total_gallons)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)
  
  top5_fuel_agencies |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    all_of(energy_columns),
    total_gallons) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Five Largest Public Transit Fuel Consumers",
    subtitle = "Total gallons consumed across all transportation modes") |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = where(is.numeric),
    decimals = 0)
```
New Jersey Transit Corporation ranked first with approximately 41.7 million gallons, followed by MTA New York City Transit with approximately 40.8 million gallons. The dataset was grouped by transit agency, and consumption values for each reported liquid and gaseous fuel type were added together to calculate total gallons consumed, then the agencies were ranked from largest to smallest.

### 8. Which five transit services have the most UPT annually? 

```{r}
NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    average_trip_length = if_else(
      total_upt > 0,
      sum_passenger_miles / total_upt,

top5_transit_services <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(AGENCY, mode) |>
```

The NTD_service dataset was grouped by transit agency and transportation mode. Annual unlinked passenger trips were summed for each agency-mode combination, and the five largest services were selected.

### 9. Which transit service in NYC has the longest average trip length? 

```{r}
longest_trip_length <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(
    str_to_lower(city) %in% c(
      "new york city",
      "brooklyn"),
    total_upt > 0) |>
  group_by(AGENCY, mode) |>
  summarize(
    total_trips = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_passenger_miles = sum(
      sum_passenger_miles,

longest_trip_length
```
MTA New York City Transit's commuter bus service had the longest average trip length in the selected results, at 17.48 miles per trip.

## Task Four: Data Integration
### How many UPTs were recorded in states where the primary energy source was nuclear power?
```{r}
names(NTD_SERVICE)

nuclear_state <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  mutate(
    state_full = str_to_title(str_trim(state)),
    primary_source = str_to_lower(str_trim(primary_source))) |>
  filter(primary_source == "nuclear") |>
  distinct(state_full)

nuclear_state

intersect(
  NTD_SERVICE$state_full |> unique(),
  nuclear_state$state_full)

nuclear_state_UPT <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  inner_join(
    nuclear_state,
    by = "state_full") |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    number_of_agencies = n_distinct(NTD_ID),
    number_of_states = n_distinct(state_full)
  )

nuclear_state_UPT
```
  The state identifiers in the NTD were standardized to full state names to ensure consistency with the EIA electricity dataset. I then created an inner join to retain only transit records from states identified as having nuclear power as their primary electricity source.

### In what metro area were the most gallons of bio-diesel used by public transit agencies?
```{r}
agency_biodiesel <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    `NTD ID` = as.character(`NTD ID`)) |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    biodiesel_gallons = sum(
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

agency_metro_area <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = as.character(NTD_ID)) |>
  distinct(NTD_ID, uza_name)

biodiesel_metro_area <- agency_biodiesel |>
  inner_join(
    agency_metro_area,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID")) |>
  group_by(uza_name) |>
  summarize(
    total_biodiesel = sum(
      biodiesel_gallons,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(total_biodiesel))

biodiesel_metro_area |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```
Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim, California, had the highest reported biodiesel consumption at 9.47 million gallons, followed by Minneapolis–St. Paul, Minnesota, at 7.13 million gallons. This analysis combines fuel consumption records with metropolitan area information using the NTD agency identification number. Biodiesel consumption is then aggregated across agencies within each urbanized area to identify the metropolitan area with the highest reported usage.


# Data Analysis
## Task Five: Calculating Total Emissions
### Compute the total emissions associated with each Agency + Mode pair.
```{r}
MODE_LOOKUP <- tibble(
  mode = c(
    "HR", "LR", "CR", "MB", "CB",
    "RB", "TB", "DR", "DT", "VP",
    "FB", "SR", "AR", "CC", "MG",
    "IP", "TR", "YR"
  ),
  mode_name = c(
    "Heavy Rail", "Light Rail", "Commuter Rail",
    "Motor Bus", "Commuter Bus", "Bus Rapid Transit",
    "Trolleybus", "Demand Response",
    "Demand Response Taxi", "Vanpool",
    "Ferryboat", "Streetcar Rail", "Alaska Railroad",
    "Cable Car", "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
    "Inclined Plane", "Aerial Tramway", "Hybrid Rail")
)

clean_NTD_energy <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  rename(
    NTD_ID = `NTD ID`,
    mode_name = Mode,
    agency = `Agency Name`) |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = as.character(NTD_ID))

STATE_LOOKUP <- tibble(
  state_abbr = state.abb,
  state_full = state.name
)

clean_NTD_service <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  left_join(
    MODE_LOOKUP,
    by = "mode") |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = as.character(NTD_ID),
    state = str_trim(state),
    state_full = case_when(
      state %in% state.name ~ state,
      str_to_upper(state) %in% state.abb ~
        state.name[match(str_to_upper(state), state.abb)],
      TRUE ~ NA_character_))

aggregated_service <- clean_NTD_service |>
  group_by(
    NTD_ID,
    mode_name,
    state_full,
    uza_name) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    passenger_miles = sum(
      sum_passenger_miles,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop")

combined_transit <- clean_NTD_energy |>
  inner_join(
    aggregated_service,
    by = c("NTD_ID", "mode_name"))

EIA_CLEAN <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  transmute(
    state_full = str_trim(state),
    CO2_MWh,
    primary_source,
    electricity_price_MWh)

combined_transit <- combined_transit |>
  left_join(
    EIA_CLEAN,
    by = "state_full")

combined_transit |>
  summarize(
    total_records = n(),
    total_agencies = n_distinct(NTD_ID),
    total_modes = n_distinct(mode_name),
    matched_electricity_emissions = sum(!is.na(CO2_MWh)),
    missing_electricity_emissions = sum(is.na(CO2_MWh))
  )

glimpse (combined_transit)

combined_transit <- combined_transit |>
  mutate(
    total_emissions_lbs =
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * 20.0 +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * 22.4 +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * 12.7 +
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * 22.45 +
      `Gallons of Ethanol` * 12.7 +
      `Gallons of Gasoline` * 19.37 +
      `Gallons of Kerosene` * 21.5 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * 12.7 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * 12.7 +
      (
        `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
        `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`
      ) / 1000 * CO2_MWh)

combined_transit |>
  summarize(
    total_agency_modes = n(),
    total_emissions_lbs = sum(
      total_emissions_lbs,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    average_emissions_lbs = mean(
      total_emissions_lbs,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_emissions = sum(
      is.na(total_emissions_lbs)))

combined_transit |>
  arrange(desc(total_emissions_lbs)) |>
  select(
    agency,
    mode_name,
    state_full,
    total_emissions_lbs
  ) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

```
These calculations produced an estimated total of 17.15 billion pounds of CO2 across 1,051 agency-mode records.

## Task Six: Relate Total Emissions and Passenger Service

```{r}
agency_performance <- combined_transit |>
  group_by(
    NTD_ID,
    agency,
    state_full,
    uza_name) |>
  summarize(
    total_emissions_lbs = sum(total_emissions_lbs,na.rm = TRUE),
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    passenger_miles = sum(passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

agency_performance <- agency_performance |>
  mutate(
    emissions_per_upt = if_else(
      total_upt > 0,
      total_emissions_lbs / total_upt,
      NA_real_),

    emissions_per_passenger_mile = if_else(
      passenger_miles > 0,
      total_emissions_lbs / passenger_miles,
      NA_real_))

agency_performance <- agency_performance |>
  mutate(
    agency_size = case_when(
      total_upt < 1000000 ~ "Small",
      total_upt < 10000000 ~ "Medium",
      TRUE ~ "Large"))

agency_rankings <- agency_performance |>
  filter(
    total_upt >= 100000,
    passenger_miles > 0,
    total_emissions_lbs >= 0)

top_upt_efficiency <- agency_rankings |>
  arrange(emissions_per_upt) |>
  select(
    agency,
    state_full,
    agency_size,
    total_upt,
    total_emissions_lbs,
    emissions_per_upt) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

top_upt_efficiency

top_mile_efficiency <- agency_rankings |>
  arrange(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |>
  select(
    agency,
    state_full,
    agency_size,
    passenger_miles,
    total_emissions_lbs,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

top_mile_efficiency

size_efficiency <- agency_rankings |>
  group_by(agency_size) |>
  summarize(
    agencies = n(),
    median_emissions_per_upt = median(emissions_per_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_emissions_per_mile = median(emissions_per_passenger_mile, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_upt = median(total_upt), .groups = "drop")

size_efficiency

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

ggplot(
  agency_rankings,
  aes(
    x = total_upt,
    y = emissions_per_upt,
    color = agency_size)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.65, size = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Small" = "#354f52",
      "Medium" = "#ea9ab2",
      "Large" = "#cd9b4e")) +
  labs(
    title = "Transit Agency Emissions Efficiency",
    subtitle = "Carbon emissions per passenger trip by annual ridership",
    x = "Annual Unlinked Passenger Trips (log scale)",
    y = "Pounds of CO2 per passenger trip",
    color = "Agency Size",
    caption = paste(
      "Source: National Transit Database and",
      "Energy Information Administration.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
A scatterplot was created to visualize the relationship between annual ridership and emissions per passenger trip.

## Task Seven: Award Winners
### The Greenest Transit Agency
```{r}

CAFE_MPG <- 28

GASOLINE_CO2_LBS_PER_GALLON <- 19.37

agency_performance <- agency_performance |>
  mutate(
    hypothetical_driving_gallons =
      passenger_miles / CAFE_MPG,

    hypothetical_driving_emissions =
      hypothetical_driving_gallons *
      GASOLINE_CO2_LBS_PER_GALLON,

    emissions_avoided =
      hypothetical_driving_emissions -
      total_emissions_lbs)
```
Agencies with lower emissions per passenger mile were considered more environmentally efficient.

### Most Emissions Avoided
```{r}
most_emissions_avoided <- agency_performance |>
  filter(
    passenger_miles > 0,
    total_upt >= 100000) |>
  arrange(desc(emissions_avoided)) |>
  select(
    agency,
    state_full,
    passenger_miles,
    total_emissions_lbs,
    hypothetical_driving_emissions,
    emissions_avoided) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

most_emissions_avoided
```
Agencies with the largest positive differences between hypothetical and actual transit emissions were identified as those with the greatest estimated emissions savings.

### Energy Consumption Kings
```{r}
median_avoided <- agency_performance |>
  filter(
    passenger_miles > 0,
    total_upt >= 100000) |>
  summarize(
    median_emissions_avoided =
      median(emissions_avoided, na.rm = TRUE))

median_avoided

agency_electricity <- combined_transit |>
  group_by(
    NTD_ID,
    agency) |>
  summarize(
    electric_kwh = sum(
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`,
      na.rm = TRUE),

    diesel_kwh = sum(
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * 37.95,
      na.rm = TRUE),

    biodiesel_kwh = sum(
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * 35,
      na.rm = TRUE),

    gasoline_kwh = sum(
      `Gallons of Gasoline` * 33.7,
      na.rm = TRUE),

    other_fuel_kwh = sum(
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * 40 +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * 33.7 +
      `Gallons of Ethanol` * 22.3 +
      `Gallons of Kerosene` * 37 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * 25 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * 26,
      na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    total_energy_kwh = electric_kwh +
      diesel_kwh +
      biodiesel_kwh +
      gasoline_kwh +
      other_fuel_kwh,

    electricity_share = if_else(
      total_energy_kwh > 0,
      electric_kwh / total_energy_kwh,
      NA_real_))

electricity_winners <- agency_electricity |>
  inner_join(
    agency_performance |>
      select(NTD_ID, total_upt),
    by = "NTD_ID") |>
  filter(
    total_upt >= 100000,
    !is.na(electricity_share)) |>
  arrange(desc(electricity_share)) |>
  select(
    agency,
    total_upt,
    electric_kwh,
    total_energy_kwh,
    electricity_share) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

electricity_winners
```
Energy consumption was converted into approximate kilowatt-hour equivalents to compare electricity use with other fuel sources. Each agency's electric energy was divided by its total estimated energy consumption to calculate an electricity share. 

### Worst Carbon Footprint Award
```{r}
worst_agencies <- agency_rankings |>
  arrange(desc(emissions_per_passenger_mile)) |>
  select(
    agency,
    state_full,
    agency_size,
    total_upt,
    passenger_miles,
    total_emissions_lbs,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

worst_agencies

median_emissions_intensity <- agency_rankings |>
  summarize(
    median_emissions_per_mile =
      median(
        emissions_per_passenger_mile,
        na.rm = TRUE))

median_emissions_intensity

```
The agency performance dataset was sorted by emissions per passenger mile in descending order to identify the agencies with the highest carbon intensity. 

### Award Summary
```{r}
award_summary <- bind_rows(

  agency_rankings |>
    slice_min(
      emissions_per_passenger_mile,
      n = 1) |>
    transmute(
      award = "Greenest Transit Agency",
      winner = agency,
      metric = emissions_per_passenger_mile,
      units = "lbs CO2 per passenger mile"),

  agency_performance |>
    slice_max(
      emissions_avoided,
      n = 1) |>
    transmute(
      award = "Most Emissions Avoided",
      winner = agency,
      metric = emissions_avoided,
      units = "lbs CO2 avoided"),

  electricity_winners |>
    slice_max(
      electricity_share,
      n = 1) |>
    transmute(
      award = "Energy Consumption Kings",
      winner = agency,
      metric = electricity_share * 100,
      units = "percent electric energy"),

  worst_agencies |>
    slice_max(
      emissions_per_passenger_mile,
      n = 1) |>
    transmute(
      award = "Worst Carbon Footprint",
      winner = agency,
      metric = emissions_per_passenger_mile,
      units = "lbs CO2 per passenger mile"))

award_summary

```
The results from the four award categories were combined into one summary table using bind_rows(). Each award includes the winning agency, its corresponding performance metric, and the measurement units.

# Transit Award Press Release
Public transportation is essential for reducing environmental impact and dependence on individual vehicles. However, transit systems also consume substantial amounts of energy and produce carbon emissions, so understanding these environmental impacts is an important step toward developing cleaner and more efficient transportation networks. A recent analysis combining data from the National Transit Database (NTD) and the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) examined the transit systems fuel consumption and released emissions. The analysis found considerable variation in the environmental impact and cost of electricity across the United States.

Hawaii had the most expensive retail electricity, at approximately $380 per megawatt-hour (MWh). California followed at $270.40 per MWh, while Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts rounded out the five most expensive states. West Virginia had the highest carbon emissions from electricity generation, producing approximately 1,912 pounds of CO2 per MWh. Kentucky, Wyoming, Missouri, and Hawaii also ranked among the five states with the most carbon-intensive electricity.Texas produced approximately 1.53 times as much CO2 per MWh as New York. 

The analysis also introduced several awards recognizing agencies based on their environmental performance.
MTA New York City Transit received the highest estimated emissions-avoided result among the qualifying agencies.

Its approximately 9.59 billion passenger miles were compared with a hypothetical scenario in which the same passenger miles were traveled in individual vehicles averaging 28 miles per gallon.This produced an estimated difference of approximately 4.89 billion pounds of CO2.

### Visualization: Most Emissions Avoided
```{r}
library (scales)
avoided_plot_data <- agency_performance |>
  filter(
    total_upt >= 100000,
    passenger_miles > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(emissions_avoided)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  select(
    agency,
    total_emissions_lbs,
    hypothetical_driving_emissions) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      total_emissions_lbs,
      hypothetical_driving_emissions),
    names_to = "transport_type",
    values_to = "emissions") |>
  mutate(
    transport_type = recode(
      transport_type,
      total_emissions_lbs = "Public Transit",
      hypothetical_driving_emissions = "Individual Driving"))

ggplot(
  avoided_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = reorder(agency, emissions),
    y = emissions,
    fill = transport_type)) +
  geom_col(
    position = "dodge",
    width = 1) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Public Transit" = "#117675",
      "Individual Driving" = "#ce6a85")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      scale = 1e-4,
      suffix = "M")) +
  labs(
    title = "The Emissions Savings of Public Transit",
    subtitle = "Actual transit emissions versus estimated individual-driving emissions",
    x = NULL,
    y = "CO2 emissions (million pounds)",
    fill = "Transportation type",
    caption = paste(
      "Driving estimate assumes 28 MPG and one person per vehicle.",
      "Sources: NTD 2025 and EIA.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Port Authority Transit Corporation and several other agencies reported 100% of their calculated energy consumption from electricity. Other agencies appearing among the top five included Staten Island Rapid Transit Operating Corporation, the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, and West Virginia University.
Electricity consumption should still be evaluated with the carbon intensity of the electricity grid to determine its overall environmental impact.

### Visualization: Energy Consumption Kings
```{r}
ggplot(
  electricity_winners,
  aes(
    x = reorder(agency, electricity_share),
    y = electricity_share)) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "#56B4E9",
    width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Transit Electrification Leaders",
    subtitle = "Electricity as a share of reported energy consumption",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Electricity share",
    caption = paste(
      "Energy sources converted to approximate kWh equivalents.",
      "Source: National Transit Database 2025.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

The winner of the Worst Carbon Footprint award was Plaquemines Port, followed in second and third place by Harbor and Terminal District, who recorded the highest emissions per passenger mile among the agencies in the qualifying analysis. Its estimated emissions intensity was approximately 23.5 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. Smaller transportation operations may face problems when serving limited passenger demand while maintaining energy-intensive services, explaining why these agencies are at the top of the list.

The findings demonstrate that public transportation has significant potential to support environmental sustainability, but that potential depends on several factors. The carbon intensity of electricity, fuel selection, passenger demand, and operational efficiency all influence the environmental performance of transit systems.

Overall, public transportation is an important part of the path toward a lower-carbon future and sustainability.
